name: Spider-silk cell
short_description: A cell — a goat mammary cell, a bacterium or a silkworm cell, depending on the route taken — carrying one or more spider genes so that it manufactures spidroin, the fibre-forming protein spiders spin their thread from. The best-known version is a goat that secretes the protein into its milk; engineered bacteria and silkworms that replace or supplement their usual silk protein with spidroin are the other two routes in active use.

textbook.1: PASS - gemini-3-pro-image. Composition is unambiguously a polarized SECRETORY CELL, not a spider: tall columnar cell, nucleus at the base, extensive slate-blue rough-ER ribbons stippled with single-dot ribosomes (verified as a real distinct colour by pixel sample: RGB ~143,149,166 vs cytoplasm ~229,214,185), apricot-orange Golgi stack, honey-gold secretory vesicles each holding one round amber droplet, and 2-3 vesicles fusing at the apical membrane releasing ROUNDED droplets/blobs above the microvilli. Zoomed crop of the apex (top ~35% of frame) confirms every released droplet is a simple circle or teardrop -- none are elongated, none touch, no thread/strand anywhere. No spider anatomy, no web, no udder, no bacterial structures, no glowing 'gene' marker in the nucleus. Small directional arrows connect the vesicle chain (ER->Golgi->apex) -- a mild deviation from car-t-cell/lentiviral-vector's arrow-free house look, kept because the subject's defining feature IS a directional pathway and the arrows aid that read without adding text/letters. Edge-pixel scan: charcoal background ~60-62 RGB on all 4 edges/rows, no border stripe. 8 label anchors sampled directly on this raw PNG (not the rasterised SVG): nucleus (178,166,190 lavender), rough_er (143,149,166 blue-grey), transport_vesicles (177,187,196 pale blue, precise dot), golgi (245,184,136 orange), secretory_vesicles (238,197,136 pale gold), apical_membrane (219,194,164 tan membrane), mitochondrion (157,186,178 teal), cytoplasm (229,214,185 cream) -- all match their intended structure's colour. Two SVG-layout bugs found and fixed after the first labelled draft: the unicode arrow '→' in 'ER → Golgi' rendered as a tofu box in the SVG font (replaced with 'to'), and long label text is fine in this style (no collision, unlike 3d/watercolor which needed row offsets).

sem.1: PASS, with an explicit gap, same reasoning as car-t-cell's CAR - gemini-3-pro-image. Single domed secretory-epithelial specimen, apical pole densely covered in short fine microvilli (false-colour amber-gold to rose), transitioning to smoother basal membrane -- zoomed crops of both the microvilli tuft and the smooth basal surface confirm crisp true 3D texture, no baked text, no scale bar. By design this style shows NO internal organelle and NO marker for the engineered protein or gene: a single secreted-protein molecule and a single transgene insertion are both many orders of magnitude below SEM resolution, so an unmodified secretory cell and this one are visually identical at this scale -- stated plainly rather than invented, matching this atlas's car-t-cell precedent for CAR. Edge-pixel scan: near-black background (~11-32 RGB, warm-tinted) on all 4 edges, no border. Per house rule, sem gets no label layer.

3d.1: FAIL - gemini-3-pro-image, attempt 1. Composition and colour legend matched the brief (polarized cell, nucleus/ER/Golgi/vesicles present, natural biological tones), BUT a zoomed crop of the apical region revealed each secretory vesicle connected to the next by a thin visible neck/tether, like beads on a string, and the same thin-strand motif ran from the topmost vesicle up through the membrane to the released droplets. This is exactly the subject's defining trap read backwards -- it could be misread as thread/fibre already forming inside the cell, which the catalogue text explicitly says does NOT happen in the cell. Discarded rather than accepted with a caveat, since this is the one property the brief called out as most likely to go wrong.
3d.2: PASS - gemini-3-pro-image, attempt 2, re-rendered with an explicit fix-prompt: every vesicle must be a separate free-floating sphere, no connecting strand of any kind. Zoomed crop of the same apical region confirms the fix: every vesicle and every released droplet is now fully separate with clear background between them, fusing individually at the membrane and popping loose as simple round/teardrop blobs -- no strand, tube, or tether anywhere. No spider, no web, no udder, no bacterial structures. Edge-pixel scan: dark charcoal-blue background ~25-33 RGB uniformly on all 4 edges, no border. 8 label anchors sampled on this raw PNG: nucleus (215,200,236 lavender), apical_membrane (201,145,86 -- lands on the gold fusion-pore neck rather than plain membrane, an honest compromise since the plain membrane in this render is a very pale near-white translucent tone that doesn't photograph as a distinct colour), secretory_vesicles (207,158,90 gold), golgi (215,140,103 orange), rough_er (125,134,156 blue-grey), mitochondrion (106,155,141 teal), cytoplasm (185,166,159 tan). transport_vesicles is the one flagged weak spot: in THIS render the small beads are ribosome-stipple dots on the ER surface, not a separately-coloured object as in the textbook version -- the closest defensible anchor (163,174,201, a bead at the ER's upper edge) is honestly noted as weakly differentiated from the ER itself, unlike the textbook style where the same structure is a clearly separate pale-blue dot. Recorded here rather than smoothed over.

watercolor.1: PASS - gemini-3-pro-image, attempt 1. Warm aged-paper wash fills the frame edge-to-edge and corner-to-corner (edge scan: paper tone ~240-250/216-228/174-192 RGB on all 4 edge rows/cols and all 4 corners, no white margin, no framed sheet-on-surface). Same polarized-cell composition: nucleus, blue-wash rough ER with ink-dot ribosomes, ochre Golgi, honey-gold secretory vesicles each with a painted amber droplet, apical microvilli fringe, and 2-3 vesicles releasing simple round/teardrop droplets above the membrane -- zoomed crop confirms no droplet is thread-like and none are connected by a line (arrows link the vesicle chain, same convention as textbook, not a physical strand). No spider, no web, no udder. Label-anchor colours are honest but softer than the other two styles, as expected of a translucent wash: nucleus (231,218,210, a pale lavender-tinted wash rather than a saturated fill -- the best obtainable point avoiding the ink cross-hatching and the nucleolus circle), rough_er (73,81,86, dark ink ribbon, clear), transport_vesicles (202,202,198, grey wash circle, clear), golgi (232,180,101, orange wash, clear), secretory_vesicles (224,186,123, gold wash, clear), apical_membrane (210,144,59, on the gold exocytosis pore, clear), mitochondrion (186,209,191, teal wash, clear), cytoplasm (245,223,178, cream paper, clear). Two SVG-layout bugs shared with the other styles were caught and fixed here too: the '→' arrow glyph in the ER label rendered as a tofu box (fixed to 'to'), and the long 'Apical membrane...' / 'Secretory vesicles...' labels initially collided when placed on the same text row on opposite margins (fixed by offsetting the right-margin rows by 110px).

reference: PASS as a disclosed analog (2026-08-23, viewed directly, both the raw download and the cleaned crop). Wikimedia Commons 'Pancreatic acinar cells - TEM.jpg', Louisa Howard/Dartmouth EM Facility, Public Domain. There is no photograph of 'a spider-silk cell' as a distinguishable object -- a transgenic goat mammary secretory cell looks like an ordinary mammary secretory cell, and no freely-licensed (non-NonCommercial) mammary-specific EM plate could be found (the one genuinely mammary-specific plate found, Honvo-Houéto et al. 2016, is CC BY-NC-SA and was rejected on licence grounds alone, per the hard no-NonCommercial rule). This pancreatic acinar cell TEM is used instead as a disclosed structural analog: it shows the same protein-secreting exocrine pathway (nucleus, extensive rough-ER 'fingerprint' whorls, mitochondria, small vesicle profiles) that a spidroin-secreting mammary cell also uses. The raw download carried a baked-in caption bar ('1Pancreas ... REMF', the Dartmouth facility watermark) confirmed by a row-brightness scan (micrograph rows mean 72-91 std 30-43 vs caption band mean 218-250 std <5); removed with a deterministic PIL crop + centre-square + resize (no AI edit, no re-illustration risk), re-scanned clean on all edges (mean 64-101, std 36-38 throughout, matching micrograph texture). The cleaned plate is captioned in the reference caption as a pancreatic acinar cell shown as an analog, explicitly not mammary tissue and not verified transgenic.
decision: polarized secretory cell with the full pathway (nucleus -> rough ER -> Golgi -> secretory vesicles -> apical exocytosis) each in a distinct legend colour; released cargo unambiguously droplet-shaped, never thread-like; no spider anywhere; 8/8 label anchors colour-verified on the raw PNG

anatomically honest single-cell surface texture; by design shows no marker for the engineered protein or gene, since both are far below SEM resolution -- stated plainly rather than invented, same reasoning as car-t-cell's CAR

attempt 1 discarded for a thin strand connecting vesicles (misreadable as thread already forming in the cell, the subject's core trap); attempt 2's explicit fix-prompt produced fully separate free-floating vesicles/droplets, verified on a zoomed crop; transport_vesicles anchor flagged as weakly colour-differentiated from the ER in this style, noted rather than hidden

aged paper fills the frame edge-to-edge and corner-to-corner (measured); same droplet-not-thread composition; softer wash colours at a few anchors, honestly reported rather than oversold as saturated fills
verified as a disclosed analog, not the microbe itself

pancreatic acinar cell TEM (Public Domain), the closest free-licensed structural analog of the rough-ER -> Golgi -> secretory-granule pathway; the one genuinely mammary-specific plate found is CC BY-NC-SA and was rejected on licence grounds; cleaned with a deterministic crop (not an AI edit) to remove a baked-in caption bar

the project's monthly Gemini spending cap was hit on the first coloring.py call (HTTP 429 'exceeded its monthly spending cap'), after all four teaching-style renders had already completed successfully. Per SKILL.md this is the hard-stop condition (distinct from a per-model daily quota) -- stopped immediately without retrying. The full scenario and prompt (a cheerful round cell character blowing bubbles of protein into a jar, deliberately keeping the no-spider/no-web/no-thread/no-goat rule even in the playful kids' page) is saved at spider-silk-cell.coloring.prompt.json, ready to render in one call once the cap is raised. This subject ships 4/5 styles + reference, no coloring page, same honest-gap precedent as feline-immunodeficiency-virus shipping 4/5.
